newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia shares mixed, bank results may boost.
newsitem.headline: Estonia shares mixed, bank results may boost.

text.p: Share prices on the Estonian stock exchange were mixed on Friday but the Talse index firmed slightly and dealers said new impetus may only come when banks' half-year results are issued at the start of July.
The market was hit by a calm ahead of a long weekend, when Estonians celebrate the midsummer holiday.
Total turnover on the main list was 46.5 million kroons and the Talse index gained 0.38 percent to 267.72.
Hansapank was the most active stock with 16 million kroons traded to gain 0.80 kroons to close at 142.00 kroons.
"Today's trade was normal for the last session before an extended break but the next two weeks should attract more interest ahead of the half year bank results," another said.
Dealers and investors are looking forward to July when banks are expected to report buoyant half-year results.
"The July figures will radically change the market and kick it off for the autumn season," another trader said.
"Several banks have said they are considering changing their profit estimates and these will be watched," one dealer said.
The free market saw trade of 17 million kroons with constuction company EMV the most active stock with an impressive gain of 6.75 kroons to close on 67.75 kroons.
The gains were made after it released five month results on Thursday, showing a profit of 7.8 million kroons.
Rakvere was traded up to end at 14.05 kroons, 0.65 kroons higher with 4.4 million kroons traded.
"Rakvere is still a good stock and as it was said, if the insiders thought it was a good stock then it is most likely still a good stock," one dealer said.
Rakvere was suspended for one day on Wednesday after the bourse announced that an insider trading investigation had started into trade of the company's stock.
